scope: web/bike/, web/index.html, .env config, Python runner, browser storage

vulnerabilities.description: API keys and access tokens stored in browser sessionStorage without encryption. Strava and intervals.icu tokens accessible to any script in same origin; XSS attack steals all tokens.
vulnerabilities.evidence: INTERVALS_KEY and STRAVA_KEY in sessionStorage; tokens used directly in Authorization headers (lines 8, 20)

vulnerabilities.description: Hand-rolled XML parser with entity expansion. Recursive decodeEntities() and ENTITIES map could be exploited by billion-laughs attack or quadratic blowup if processing untrusted ZWO/MRC files.
vulnerabilities.evidence: decodeEntities(s) at line 24 recursively processes entity references; no entity depth limit or size cap enforced
vulnerabilities.scenario: Malicious ZWO file with nested entity definitions causes CPU/memory exhaustion during parseXml()
vulnerabilities.cve_pattern: CWE-776 (Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References)

vulnerabilities.description: Unfiltered error objects logged to console. Network error messages may contain sensitive URLs, HTTP headers, or response body fragments if fetch fails.
vulnerabilities.evidence: console.log('Request exception:', error) at lines 45 and 79; error.message exposed directly
vulnerabilities.scenario: Failed fetch to /paceforge/api/sync leaks full URL and any error details in browser console accessible to attacker XSS payload
vulnerabilities.cve_pattern: CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File)

vulnerabilities.description: Ride data (power, HR, cadence, timestamp) stored in localStorage as plain JSON without integrity verification. Browser storage is world-readable by any script on same origin.
vulnerabilities.evidence: localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify({...})) at line 62; no HMAC/signature
vulnerabilities.scenario: Malicious script modifies ride data in localStorage; corrupted data uploads to Strava, affecting athlete's training log

vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted JSON loaded from localStorage via ls() helper without schema validation. Arbitrary objects could be injected to corrupt app state.
vulnerabilities.evidence: function ls(key, fallback) { ... JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key)) } at line 45; no schema check before use in loadProfile() or S.profile
vulnerabilities.scenario: Attacker injects {ftp: 999999, wprime_j: 0} into pf-bike-profile; app uses invalid FTP for calculations, breaking coaching logic

vulnerabilities.description: Session auth uses cookie-based scoping (PF_COOKIE_PATH) with no mention of CSRF token validation. Runner endpoints accept state-changing operations (plan, sync, recalibrate) without CSRF check.
vulnerabilities.evidence: Auth section describes session cookies but no CSRF token strategy documented; runner.py accepts POST /plan, /sync, /recalibrate
vulnerabilities.scenario: Attacker tricks athlete into visiting malicious site; embedded form auto-POSTs /paceforge/api/plan?goal=HALF_MARATHON, modifying training plan without consent

vulnerabilities.description: localStorage namespace derived from location.pathname without robust normalization. Path traversal or special characters could cause key collision between athletes if running multiple instances.
vulnerabilities.evidence: const NS = location.pathname.replace(/\/(index\.html)?$/, '') || '/' at line 7; uses raw pathname
vulnerabilities.scenario: If URL is /paceforge/../pf/alice/, NS becomes different than /paceforge/, keys overlap and data leaks between instances

vulnerabilities.description: No evidence of security headers (STS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) configured in runner. Browser cannot enforce same-origin-policy strictness.
vulnerabilities.evidence: CLAUDE.md documents runner.py serves /web and /data but no headers section in runner code
vulnerabilities.scenario: Missing CSP allows XSS payloads to execute inline scripts; missing X-Frame-Options allows clickjacking; missing STS allows downgrade to HTTP

vulnerabilities.description: API responses from Garmin and Strava not validated against schema before use. Malformed or malicious responses could corrupt app state.
vulnerabilities.evidence: loadJSON('bike/profile.json') returns unvalidated objects assigned directly to S.profile (line ~97)
vulnerabilities.scenario: Garmin API hijack or MITM returns {ftp: 'string'} instead of number; downstream code fails or behaves unexpectedly

vulnerabilities.description: Strava credentials (STRAVA_CLIENT_ID, STRAVA_CLIENT_SECRET, STRAVA_REFRESH_TOKEN) documented in .env. Risk: env file committed, leaked in shell history, or exposed in logs.
vulnerabilities.evidence: .env.example lines 6-8 show STRAVA_* and PACEFORGE_GARMIN_PASSWORD examples
vulnerabilities.scenario: Developer accidentally commits .env to repo; GitHub actions logs expose STRAVA_CLIENT_SECRET during build

vulnerabilities.description: Mock trainer uses Math.random() for noise injection. While non-critical for a test harness, JS Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and should never seed real data.
vulnerabilities.evidence: const noise = amp => (Math.random() + ...) * amp at line 9
vulnerabilities.scenario: If mock trainer code ever runs in production, user-facing random values are predictable
vulnerabilities.cve_pattern: CWE-338 (Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator)

recommendations: CRITICAL (Day 1): Remove sessionStorage for sensitive tokens. Implement in-memory token cache; require user re-auth for uploads (or use server-side auth proxy).
HIGH: Add entity expansion limit to XML parser (max 10 nesting levels, total size cap 1MB). Validate MRC/ZWO files server-side before processing.
HIGH: Sanitize error logging. Replace console.log(error) with console.error('Request failed') only; never log error.message or full objects.
HIGH: Add CSRF tokens to all state-changing endpoints (/plan, /sync, /recalibrate). Verify token on runner.py POST handlers.
HIGH: Add security headers to runner: Content-Security-Policy (self, no inline), Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=31536000), X-Frame-Options (DENY), X-Content-Type-Options (nosniff).
MEDIUM: Sign localStorage data with HMAC before write. Validate signature on read; discard corrupted entries.
MEDIUM: Implement JSON schema validation for all external data (Garmin responses, localStorage loads). Reject mismatches.
MEDIUM: Normalize and validate location.pathname in ns.js; use URL API if available (URL(location).pathname).
MEDIUM: Add .env.example to .gitignore patterns in CI; scan commits for leaked secrets (git-secrets, TruffleHog).
LOW: Add optional HTTPS-only flag to runner; enforce on Azure Caddy frontend.
LOW: Document GARMIN_PASSWORD should never be persisted; one-time login only (already correct, but add comment to .env.example).

auth_findings.session_cookie: Scoped by PF_COOKIE_PATH; httpOnly and Secure flags not mentioned — verify in runner.py
auth_findings.garmin_oauth: Refresh token stored in env; TTL ~1 year. No rotation policy documented.
auth_findings.strava_oauth: Manual token in sessionStorage; no refresh flow. Requires re-auth when token expires.
auth_findings.mfa: Garmin supports optional MFA during login; no bypass mechanisms evident. Good.

compliant_areas: Web Bluetooth API inherently requires user interaction (trainer.js, hr.js)
No SQL injection risk (Pydantic-based, no raw SQL visible)
No hardcoded API keys in source code (only in .env, properly gitignored)
priority_fixes: 1. SessionStorage token theft: move auth to server-side proxy (2-3h)
2. XML entity expansion: add parser limits (30min)
3. Error logging disclosure: sanitize console output (15min)
summary: PaceForge has 10 findings (3 high, 4 medium, 3 low). Main risks: browser storage of API tokens vulnerable to XSS, missing CSRF tokens on state-changing endpoints, unvalidated XML parsing, and inadequate error logging control. None are critical for a single-athlete local instance, but multi-athlete deployments (planned sharing feature) amplify session/CSRF/storage isolation issues. Recommend implementing fixes in priority order before sharing instances with friends.
